entities.summary: Diana degli Andalò, OP, was a Dominican nun who founded a convent in Italy dedicated to Saint Agnes. Born in the 12th century, she spent her life devoted to prayer and service. The convent she established became a center of learning and spiritual growth, attracting scholars and pilgrims from across Europe. Diana's legacy extends to the present day, as her convent remains a significant cultural and historical landmark. In 1862, the convent was converted into a museum, preserving the history and art of the medieval period.
